title: Ueno on Foot
blurb: Walk Ueno under the real sun: up the park's steps past Saigo and his dog, round Shinobazu Pond to Bentendo, up the lantern-lined approach to Toshogu's gilt hall, and down into Ameyoko's market.

npcs.name: Noriko 典子
idle: Five museums, a concert hall and a zoo on one hill. Most people only see the pandas.
The cherries here are the city's clock: when they open, half of Tokyo has a picnic under them. {time}.

npcs.name: Daichi 大地
idle: Tuna, crab, salmon roe! In December you can't move in here.
My grandfather sold sweets from a box under the tracks in 1946. Ame, sweets: that's the name. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Sota 颯太
idle: Rowing boats, pedal boats, swan boats. The swans are the ones couples fight about.
There's an old story that couples who row here together split up. Business is still good.

npcs.name: Aoi 葵
idle: Toshogu is Tokugawa Ieyasu's shrine. The gold is real leaf; we redid it in 2013.
The peony garden opens in winter: peonies under straw hats in the snow.

quests.title: Ueno
talk: Welcome to Ueno! I'm Noriko; I guide at the National Museum on weekends.
This was the gate to the north: the trains from Tohoku came in here. Across the road is Ameyoko. Find Daichi; he shouts louder than anyone.

quests.title: Ameyoko
talk: Ameyoko: fish on one side, sweets on the other, shoes upstairs, beer under the tracks.
Go and see the gate at the station end. Then come back hungry.

steps.text: Look down Ameyoko from its gate
Meet Saigo and his dog up the steps

quests.title: Shinobazu Pond
talk: Shinobazu Pond: three ponds, one for lotus, one for boats, one for cormorants.
Walk out to Bentendo on its island. The goddess of the hall plays the biwa; musicians come to her for luck.

quests.title: The gilt hall
talk: Up the approach between the lanterns to the Konjiki-den. Gold leaf, black lacquer, 1651.
From the approach you can see the old pagoda over the zoo's fence. It's older than the hall.

spots.name: Bentendo 弁天堂
lines: Benzaiten, goddess of water, music and luck: the island was built for her in the 1600s, after Lake Biwa's Chikubushima.
The hall burned in the 1945 air raids; this one is from 1958. People still come to pray for luck in the arts.

spots.name: Shinobazu Pond 不忍池
lines: In July and August the leaves stand a metre high and the flowers open at dawn. Now they're brown and dry, waiting for spring.
This was an inlet of Tokyo Bay once. The sea went out; the pond stayed.

spots.name: Kan'ei-ji pagoda 五重塔
lines: Rebuilt in 1639, it has outlived the shogun's temple it belonged to, the 1868 battle on this hill, two earthquakes and the war.
It stands inside the zoo now. The pandas live a short walk away.

spots.name: Ueno Toshogu 上野東照宮
lines: The Konjiki-den, the golden hall, 1651: Tokugawa Ieyasu's shrine. Gold leaf over the walls, black lacquer on the posts.
The lanterns along the approach were given by the daimyo, each with his name on it. Count them; there are about two hundred.

spots.name: Saigo Takamori 西郷隆盛像
lines: Saigo Takamori with his dog Tsun, 1898. He led the samurai who gave Edo back to the emperor, then rebelled and died.
His widow said at the unveiling that he never dressed like that in public. Everyone meets here anyway.

spots.name: Ameyoko アメ横
lines: Ameyoko: after the war, a black market under the tracks. Ame for the sweets sold here, or for America, for the army's goods.
Every December the whole of Tokyo comes for New Year's crab and salmon roe. Half a kilometre, elbow to elbow.
Tuna, tuna! Three for a thousand!
Blocks! Take two, I'll throw in roe.
